cds.title: Colorado Mesa University Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF)

ipeds_ef.title: IPEDS Fall Enrollment 2023 (EF2023A): undergraduate total and U.S. nonresident headcount

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (fall 2025): applicants = 5,886 men + 7,279 women; admits = 4,879 men + 6,067 women (the unknown-sex admit cell is suppressed, 'C or t', and unknown-sex applicants are 0). CMU reports an open admission policy for all students (with selective admission to some programs). The in-state/out-of-state/international split of applicants and admits is suppressed in the Common Data Set, so no international admit rate can be shown; degree-seeking nonresident undergraduates were 101 (the total-undergraduate nonresident cell is suppressed). The GPA breakdown is only printed for the 'students who submitted scores' column; the average GPA of 3.38 covers all who submitted a GPA. Undergraduate enrollment is the 'Total All Undergraduates' figure (9,459).

cds_test_policy.notes: From the Common Data Set (fall 2027): SAT or ACT 'not required for admission, but considered if submitted'.

cost.notes: First-year costs for 2026-27 from the Common Data Set. Its tuition figures (11,480 in-state; 29,325 out-of-state and international) equal the per-credit rates ($336.90 / $931.70) plus the $45.80 per-credit required fee, times 30 credits, so they appear to include required fees; required fees are therefore not shown separately. Food and housing on campus $13,904 (housing $7,850 + meal plan $6,054). CMU's international admissions page estimates $42,259 per year for undergraduates (tuition and fees $23,460 for 24 in-person credits, residence hall and meal plan $13,151, health insurance $1,148, books and other $4,500)
